intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene (600465) on chromosome 10q21.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 (MRT37) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ANK3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: Homozygous ANK3 mutation in a consanguineous family with ID.

checks.claim: The ANK3 gene is located on chromosome 10q21.
checks.evidence_quote: AnkyrinG, encoded by the ANK3 gene, is involved in neuronal development and signaling.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that restates the gene; it is not stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 is a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by severe intellectual disability. It comes with significant behavioral problems, including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and aggressive behavior.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by severe intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract describes the family with the homozygous mutation as having 'moderate intellectual disability (ID)', not severe.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 is associated with significant behavioral problems.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 includes attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The abstract says 'ADHD-like phenotype', not ADHD.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-37 includes aggressive behavior.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. Aggressive behavior is not mentioned in the abstract; it may be in the full text.

paragraphs.text: Iqbal et al. (2013) described a consanguineous Pakistani family in which several sibs had severe intellectual disability. Affected individuals also had attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and behavioral problems, including aggression. Sleep disturbance was also reported.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) described a consanguineous Pakistani family with MRT37.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID)
checks.explanation: The abstract gives a consanguineous family; Pakistani origin is not stated.

checks.claim: Several sibs in the consanguineous Pakistani family described by Iqbal et al. (2013) had severe intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the family had 'moderate intellectual disability (ID)', not severe. The number of sibs is not given.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the Pakistani family described by Iqbal et al. (2013) had attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: The abstract says ADHD-like phenotype; Pakistani origin is not stated.

checks.claim: Affected individuals in the Pakistani family described by Iqbal et al. (2013) had behavioral problems, including aggression.
checks.evidence_quote: an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems
checks.explanation: Behavioral problems are stated; aggression is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: Sleep disturbance was reported in affected individuals in the Pakistani family described by Iqbal et al. (2013).
checks.explanation: The abstract attributes 'sleeping problems' to the translocation patient, not to the consanguineous family.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of MRT37 in the family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of MRT37 in the Pakistani family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation
checks.explanation: Consanguinity plus a homozygous mutation implies recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not state the inheritance pattern or the Pakistani origin.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Pakistani family with MRT37, Iqbal et al. (2013) found a homozygous truncating (frameshift) mutation in the ANK3 gene. The mutation lay in the large exon that is specific to the longest, neuron-specific isoform of ankyrin-G, so it was predicted to affect only that isoform. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the family. In the same report, Iqbal et al. (2013) described an unrelated patient with intellectual disability and behavioral abnormalities who carried a balanced translocation disrupting ANK3. They proposed that ANK3 disruption sits at the crossroads of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) identified a homozygous frameshift (truncating) mutation in the ANK3 gene in affected members of a consanguineous Pakistani family with MRT37.
checks.evidence_quote: in a consanguineous family with moderate intellectual disability (ID), an ADHD-like phenotype and behavioral problems, we identified a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: Supported apart from the Pakistani origin, which the abstract does not state.

checks.claim: The ANK3 frameshift mutation in the Pakistani family with MRT37 is located in the large exon specific to the longest, neuron-specific isoform of ankyrin-G.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The longest isoform is stated; the 'large exon' and 'neuron-specific' details are not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The ANK3 frameshift mutation in the Pakistani family with MRT37 was predicted to affect only the longest, neuron-specific isoform of ankyrin-G.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous truncating frameshift mutation in the longest isoform of the same gene
checks.explanation: The abstract implies an effect on the longest isoform, in contrast with 'all isoforms' in the translocation patient; neuron-specific is not stated.

checks.claim: The ANK3 frameshift mutation segregated with MRT37 in the Pakistani family reported by Iqbal et al. (2013).
checks.explanation: Segregation analysis is not described in the abstract; it may be in the full text.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) described an unrelated patient with intellectual disability and behavioral abnormalities who carried a balanced translocation disrupting ANK3.
checks.evidence_quote: In a patient with a borderline intelligence, severe attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism and sleeping problems, all isoforms of the ANK3 gene, were disrupted by a balanced translocation.
checks.explanation: The patient is described as having borderline intelligence rather than intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Iqbal et al. (2013) proposed that ANK3 disruption lies at the crossroads of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous and heterozygous disruptions of ANK3: at the crossroads of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.
